_comment: Shape of the licence gate a product used for its .NET, npm and Python dependencies. Every entry carries a reason: an allow-list nobody can explain is a list nobody can maintain. Not wired into any template here; see the KNOWN-GAPS section of the README for why it was taken out of the PR pipelines.
_whyDenyIsSeparate: An allow-list answers 'is this known'. The deny list answers 'is this the specific thing we decided against', and gives a better error than 'unknown package' when someone adds the paid edition of a component whose free edition was chosen deliberately.
_whyNpmIsCheckedByLicence: NuGet lock files carry no licence, so NuGet packages are matched by NAME. npm lock files declare a licence for almost every package, so npm is matched by LICENCE: one Angular workspace pulls well over a thousand packages, and a name list of that size is a gate somebody eventually turns off.

allow.reason: PostgreSQL driver and EF provider, PostgreSQL Licence (BSD-like).

deny.reason: The grid component is used under its MIT community edition. The enterprise edition is a per-developer paid licence nobody bought; needing it is a commercial decision, not a package install.

allow.reason: Weak, FILE-level copyleft, and a deliberate decision: reached only through a build-time CSS tool that is neither modified nor shipped. Patching one of its files would oblige publishing that file; revisit this entry if that ever happens.

deny.reason: Network copyleft: fatal for a SaaS product, serving it over a network triggers the obligation.
Not open source; its service-source obligation targets exactly this kind of product.

exceptions.evidence: The published package omits the licence field; the upstream repository carries an MIT LICENSE file.
exceptions.whySafe: Build-time only, reached transitively through a local dev server; never shipped.
exceptions.reason: Pinned to a version on purpose: a package that omitted its licence at 0.5.0 may declare something else at 0.6.0, and an unpinned exception would cover that silently.
